title: Step 2: strictly decreasing radii from a property holding at arbitrarily small scales
statement: Let Q be any property of real numbers and let δ₀ > 0. Suppose that for every δ > 0 there is a real number ρ with 0 < ρ < δ and Q(ρ). Then there is a sequence (ρ_k)_{k∈ℕ} of real numbers such that ρ_k > 0 and ρ_k < δ₀ for every k, (ρ_k) is strictly decreasing, ρ_k → 0 as k → ∞, and Q(ρ_k) holds for every k.
lean_statement: ∀ (Q : ℝ → Prop) (δ₀ : ℝ), 0 < δ₀ → (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ρ < δ ∧ Q ρ) → ∃ ρs : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 < ρs k) ∧ (∀ k, ρs k < δ₀) ∧ StrictAnti ρs ∧ Tendsto ρs atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ k, Q (ρs k)
